calls.reason: Pre-post papers (projected diffusion, ECI sampling) give provable guarantees for narrow, specified constraints but not for truthfulness or general physics. Whether that defeats the categorical wording turns on scope, so the evidence is mixed.
OpenAI's launch post concedes the deployed Sora often produces unrealistic physics. The cited Mashable report describes Brownlee finding objects that vanish and movement that is wrong.

This forecast has no deadline, and no study isolates the effect of more data on Sora. The Kang et al. scaling study tests other models, and Sora 2's reported gains do not separate data from other changes.
The forecast is open-ended. OpenAI reports better physics in Sora 2, while a 2026 benchmark that includes Sora 2 Pro still finds frequent coherence failures. Neither result settles 'wouldn't'.

Kang et al. find out-of-distribution failure but perfect in-distribution learning. Sora's training also uses generated captions, so it is not a clean test of learning from sense data alone. The claim is broad and largely rhetorical.

'Never' has no deadline. A 2026 benchmark with Sora 2 Pro finds coherence at only about 60%, which suggests the problem persists but cannot settle a permanent forecast, and the test is not purely about object permanence.
